% xr-hyper, hyperref, then xr, as when a document adds xr after a setup
% that loads xr-hyper. xr's \externaldocument is the one used. The page
% builds, and each reference prints as with xr alone: from an .aux that
% LaTeX wrote under hyperref, whose \externaldocument gives the URL of its
% PDF, its number, page, name, and \autoref as in the PDF, with no link and
% no URL; from an .aux that tex4ht wrote under hyperref, with its .xref, a
% link to that document's page.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{xr-hyper}
\usepackage{hyperref}
\usepackage{xr}
\externaldocument[X-]{test-xr/latex}[https://example.org/ext.pdf]
\externaldocument[H-]{test-xrboth/hyper-xr}
\begin{document}
CaseX \ref{X-ss}, page \pageref{X-front}, named \nameref{X-thm},
auto \autoref{X-thm}.

CaseY \ref{H-oss}, auto \autoref{H-oss}.

\section{Here}\label{here}
Local \ref{here}.
\end{document}
